cases.title: National / Delhi: follow the Navy lease beyond the signed contract
cases.question: Can the publicly announced foreign-supplier lease be reconciled to service acceptance, variation orders and payments?
cases.summary: The August 17 MoD release names GA-ASI and a roughly ₹1,943 crore 30-month lease. Delhi is the signing/administration context; this is national procurement, not a Delhi incident or a corruption allegation.

observations.text: A signed contract is publicly reported for two systems for 30 months; the amount is a contract commitment, not a paid or lost amount.
Additional Secretary and DG(Acquisition) A.Anbarasu is identified as present at signing; presence does not establish personal allocation, ownership or benefit.

counterevidence.text: MoD gives an operational capability purpose. The release contains no finding of overpricing, default or improper payment; different lease support bundles cannot be compared as bare aircraft unit prices.

cases.title: National / Delhi–Mumbai: reconcile write-offs with recovery cohorts
cases.question: Which public records can distinguish accounting write-offs, legally waived liabilities, settlements and actual recovery?
cases.summary: A July 20 parliamentary reply answers a 15-year corporate-loan question using 12 FY rows for a different RBI reporting category. Delhi and Mumbai denote national policy and banking administration; the amounts are not city allocations.

observations.text: FY 2025–26 provisional Large–Industry & Services domestic figures are ₹15,213 crore written off and ₹4,456 crore actual recoveries. These annual flows are not a matched vintage.
Separately, the March 31,2026 CRILC snapshot counts 1,249 borrowers with total written-off amounts of₹100 crore or more, totaling₹4,19,380 crore across all borrower types.
The reply cites section 45 E confidentiality for borrower-level CRILC information; it does not supply names that can be joined to a minister or beneficiary.

counterevidence.text: The reply says write-off is an accounting procedure and borrower liabilities persist. Actual debt forgiveness, negotiated settlement and insolvency haircut need their own orders and cash records.
Recoveries during a year can concern earlier write-offs; ratios of the two annual columns do not establish cohort recovery performance or personal benefit.

nextRecords.record: Nonprovisional FY 2025–26 aggregate table and definitions
nextRecords.purpose: Track revisions without silently mixing categories or time bases.

cases.title: National / Delhi: verify beneficial-control reporting after the FDI rule change
cases.question: Do the revised investment reports preserve the ownership aggregation and effective-control tests required by the Gazette?
cases.summary: The August 21 government update reports 29 proposed investments worth₹4,895.65 crore under the revised framework. The public summary does not identify their investees. This is a national policy/control-monitoring case indexed at Delhi, not an allegation against those investors.

observations.text: The Gazette notification dated May 1 was published May 2,2026, with commencement on publication; PN 2 itself deferred commencement to FEMA notification.
Cumulative direct/indirect rights, control over the investor and ultimate effective control over the investee remain explicit tests. A small nominal shareholding alone does not decide the route.
The reported₹4,895.65 crore is proposed FDI across 29 reports as ofAugust 20, not certified incoming cash or expenditure.

counterevidence.text: Government states the purpose is clarity and faster lawful investment; the framework retains sector caps, control tests, reporting and prior approval for covered ownership changes.
The Gazette expressly treats multilateral banks/funds of which India is a member differently for this rule. A World Bank or similar connection alone is not evidence of a prohibited route.

nextRecords.holder: DPIIT / RBI / Department of Economic Affairs
